summary: Draft Session Manager Kernel record. `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog` sits under `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel`, has an explicit repo-doc default of `0`, is absent on the observed clean baseline, produced an exact current-build string hit in `ntoskrnl.exe`, survived a write-and-reboot lightweight runtime batch as a candidate value of `1`, has dedicated live KVM local-KD proof that `KiForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog` exists on the running current build with value `0`, and now has a current-build INIT descriptor row that binds the registry value name to the same live global RVA. A later QGA WPR boot run failed to save the requested target ETL, but the raw WPR System Collector ETL converted successfully and still produced zero exact `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog` hits. The lane is real, but still lacks an exact runtime registry read and proven non-default semantics.

validation_proof.exact_quote_or_path: Docs/system/system.md assigns `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog = 0` under `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel`, and later baseline, string, runtime, and live KD follow-ups keep the same value on the current-build research lane.
validation_proof.notes: This is enough to document the record as a real current-build candidate; the remaining blocker is exact reader/seeding proof rather than missing validation structure.

setting.name: Force Bugcheck For DPC Watchdog
setting.casual_explanation: This appears to be a kernel-level Session Manager setting related to DPC watchdog bugcheck behavior. It is not a normal end-user setting and is being tracked as a research candidate.
setting.why_people_change_it: Kernel researchers may inspect this value when investigating DPC watchdog policy, watchdog escalation behavior, or kernel timing diagnostics.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The value has a stronger than usual docs-first evidence chain, but it is still kernel-adjacent and not safe for general use. Current evidence is enough for a draft record, not for a published tweak. The newest QGA/WPR raw-collector salvage run adds a targeted no-hit, not a runtime-read proof.
setting.professional_notes: Repo docs assign `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog = 0` and tie the value to `KiForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog`. The docs-first kernel routing pass later kept it inside the `session-manager-kernel` exact-hit batch. The observed clean baseline then confirmed that `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel` exists while the value itself is absent. The broad current-build string batch found an exact Unicode hit for `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog` in `ntoskrnl.exe`. A later tools-hardened lightweight runtime lane wrote all 21 `Session Manager\\Kernel` batch values, including `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog = 1`, rebooted once, preserved shell health, and still returned `no-hit` for this specific candidate in the ETW-derived query surface. A dedicated KVM local-KD follow-up then resolved the live DPC watchdog symbol cluster and directly read `nt!KiForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog = 0` on the running current build, which aligns with the repo-doc default and is stronger than docs-plus-string evidence alone. A later host-side PE scan of the current-build `ntoskrnl.exe` found an INIT descriptor row in the `Session Manager\\Kernel` context that binds the `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog` value-name string to static RVA `0xFC5E84`, matching the live KD RVA for `nt!KiForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog`. The QGA WPR boot lane was then retried against the exact value name; the wrapper observed a real reboot but failed to save the requested target ETL, while the raw WPR System Collector ETL still converted to an 87 MB CSV with zero exact `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog` hits. That raw-collector salvage result reduces transport ambiguity but does not close `runtime_no_read`. The next proof step is no longer symbol existence or current-build registry seeding; it is an exact runtime trace or debugger-assisted call path that proves when the descriptor is consumed and whether a non-default registry value is an active override.

evidence.title: Boot WPR captured Session Manager Kernel QueryValue context but no exact runtime read for ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog
evidence.summary: A KVM boot WPR registry trace produced a saved ETL and a large tracerpt CSV. The retained context window shows `Open` for `Session Manager\\Kernel` followed by `QueryValue` for `DefaultHeteroCpuPolicy`, proving this CSV format can render exact value-name reads under the same key family. Whole-file filtering found no exact `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog` hit, so this lane is retained as stronger negative runtime evidence and no exact runtime read proof.

evidence.title: Seeded default Registry-only boot WPR still found no exact runtime read for ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog
evidence.summary: A Registry-only WPR boot trace seeded `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog = 0` before reboot, captured a saved ETL and tracerpt CSV, then rolled the value back to its original absent state. The target exact-hit filter still returned `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog = 0` hits, so this is stronger negative runtime evidence and no exact runtime read proof.

evidence.title: Current-build INIT descriptor binds ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog to KiForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog
evidence.summary: A host-side current-build `ntoskrnl.exe` INIT descriptor scan found the `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog` UTF-16 string in the `INIT` section, one descriptor row at file offset `0xbf25b8`, and a nearby `Session Manager\\Kernel` key context. The row points at static target VA `0x140FC5E84`, whose RVA `0xFC5E84` matches the live KD RVA for `nt!KiForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog`; this closes the current-build static registry-seeding layer while leaving exact runtime registry trace evidence unresolved.

evidence.title: DPC/timer ETW registry trace completed but found no ForceBugcheck target hit
evidence.summary: A KVM guest DPC/timer ETW run collected Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-Registry, Kernel-General, Kernel-Power, and Kernel-Processor-Power providers for 45 seconds, produced a 5.7 MB ETL and 57 MB tracerpt XML, and successfully uploaded the trace summary. The target filter found zero hits for `ForceBugcheck`, so this is retained as additional negative runtime evidence and does not close the exact runtime-read blocker.

evidence.title: QGA-launched WPR boot run left raw collector ETL with no ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog hit
evidence.summary: A QGA-launched WPR boot run observed a real reboot but failed to save the requested target ETL. The raw WPR System Collector ETL left in the run directory was still convertible through tracerpt; the 28 MB ETL produced an 87 MB CSV, and exact filtering found zero `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog` hits. This is raw-collector salvage negative evidence and does not close the exact runtime-read blocker.

decision.why: The candidate is strong enough for a schema-backed draft because it has a repo-doc default, observed baseline state, current-build string hit, a real write-and-reboot runtime lane, dedicated live current-build KD proof that the kernel global exists at value `0`, and a current-build INIT descriptor binding from `ForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog` to the same global. A QGA-launched raw WPR System Collector salvage run also found zero exact value-name hits after a real reboot. It is not ready for validation because the exact runtime registry read and non-default semantics remain unproven.

open_questions: Can a future boot/runtime trace capture the exact registry query or descriptor-consumption path that seeds `KiForceBugcheckForDpcWatchdog` from `Session Manager\\Kernel`?
Does a present `REG_DWORD = 1` alter behavior only at boot or also post-boot?

Did the raw WPR collector miss the value because the descriptor is consumed outside the retained profile, or because the current build no longer reads the registry value at boot?
